problem: Navigation policies are trained with hand-designed simulator rewards/meta-data or costly human teleoperation demonstrations, so they cannot autonomously learn or adapt in a new real-world environment without external feedback. Curiosity-based self-supervised exploration also tends to roam within limited regions.
motivation: A home robot should learn (or keep adapting) its navigation skill in its own house using only on-board observations, with no reset function and no human labels. This needs both data-efficient learning without rewards and exploration that covers the whole house so the goal-conditioned policy generalizes.
key_idea: Build an online dynamic topological graph memory of on-board observations that simultaneously serves as exploration goal selector, pseudo-reward and imitation-data generator for training an image-goal policy, and as a planner at test time.
insight: The graph provides an explicit, count-based search direction, which yields more consistent exploration than curiosity modules (RND, forward dynamics) that roam repeatedly over a few regions (coverage figure, GridWorld FourRooms near-uniform state distribution). Graph-derived topological-distance rewards plus IL on stored shortest edge trajectories make label-free training work where PPO with a dense simulator reward and sparse-reward training fail. Pose noise ablation (tau 0.1 to 0.3) shows only a small drop (SR 55.0 to 51.7) since the value function used for localization does not depend on pose. SPL lags DAggre because the agent must pass through every waypoint node.
method: Node iteration: each node stores RGB image, noisy pose, visit count, and ResNet18 feature; observations are kept only if the YOLOv5 detection-confidence sum exceeds a threshold and pose distance plus alpha times negative cosine visual similarity to existing nodes exceeds a threshold, keeping the graph sparse.

Edge iteration: the agent localizes itself on the graph by visual and pose similarity; edges (binary reachability) carry the most efficient trajectory tau_ij and visit counts; rarely used edges are periodically pruned.
Active exploration: goal nodes are sampled with softmax over negative visit counts (p_i ∝ exp(-gamma c_i)), so the agent moves to novel/uncertain nodes and the graph grows to cover the house.

Self-supervised reward: r = topological distance reward (change in graph path length from previous vs current node to goal node) + navigation-trajectory reward (bonus for first-time passed nodes) + success reward from image similarity.
IL from graph: stored optimal edge trajectories serve as demonstrations; cross-entropy plus KL regularization to the old policy (PPG-style) is interleaved with PPO.

Hierarchical test-time policy: localize start and goal images in the graph using the learned value function, BFS shortest path over nodes, and the local goal-conditioned policy (ResNet18 frozen, fusion FC 512/256, GRU 256) navigates node to node.

setting.backbone: ResNet18 (ImageNet pre-trained, frozen) + FC + GRU policy trained from scratch with PPO+IL; YOLOv5 for node filtering
setting.training_data: Only self-collected on-board experience in each scene (about 1M interaction steps per scene, no labels, rewards or demonstrations from the simulator)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + noisy relative pose estimate
setting.simulator: Habitat with Gibson scenes (8 scenes); GridWorld FourRooms for a toy example
setting.privileged: none at test time (goal image only); the simulator meta-data is used only by baselines

numbers.eval_set_note: per-scene results on Nicut, Dryville, Placida, Roane, Adrian, Ballou, Mesic, Nemacolin; each trained per scene
numbers.backbone: ResNet18 + GRU policy with graph planner
numbers.extra: trained per scene, no external feedback
numbers.evidence: Table 'Performance on indoor navigation tasks' (Ours rows); scene split not officially specified

numbers.extra: policy trained on only 59/64 nodes, tested on all 256 states

numbers_note: Main table gives per-scene values as fractions (printed 0-1, kept as printed); no averaged benchmark result. Coverage results are in figures only. The pose-noise ablation (tau=0.1/0.2/0.3: SR 55.0/54.6/51.7, SPL 52.1/51.6/49.1, distance 2.29/2.46/2.57) is average across scenes.
results: DGMem outperforms BClone, PPO with dense reward and sparse-reward training in success rate and distance to goal on all 8 Gibson scenes, and beats DAggre (uses expert planner) in SR in most scenes (e.g. Nicut 0.75 vs 0.67, Adrian 0.61 vs 0.37, Nemacolin 0.54 vs 0.05). DAggre has better SPL in several scenes (e.g. Nicut 0.75 vs 0.72). Exploration coverage is higher than Random, Straight, DP and RND.
limitations: Static BFS path planning forces visiting every waypoint node, making paths suboptimal (lower SPL than DAggre)
Only evaluated in simulation on 8 Gibson scenes with per-scene training, using noisy simulated pose; no real robot; single-task (image-goal)
Hyperparameters not searched carefully; results only on discrete-action, static scenes with no baselines from other recent image-goal methods
